extracted.intended_audience: researchers and investigators applying to the PCRP (prostate cancer grant applicants), including early-career/mentored investigators, research program managers, and program stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the Prostate Cancer Research Program's funding priorities and strategic goals that applications should address, including desired research types (innovation, translational, mentored), target outcomes (clinical relevance, quality of life, reducing disparities), and alignment with PCRP overarching challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly innovative, groundbreaking research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCRP specifically seeks proposals that are novel and breakthrough in approach; the program originated to foster novel approaches to biomedical research and emphasizes innovation as a primary characteristic of fundable work.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-impact research with near-term clinical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund high-impact research that has near-term clinical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCRP prioritizes projects likely to have measurable clinical impact in the near term, particularly those that can improve outcomes for patients, service members, veterans, and caregivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support the next generation through mentored research
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the next generation of prostate cancer investigators through mentored research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program funds mentored training and career-development mechanisms to expand capacity and cultivate early-career investigators; examples and announcements note 'mentored science to expand capacity for impactful prostate cancer research.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Support resources that facilitate translational research
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund resources that will facilitate translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCRP supports infrastructure and resource projects (e.g., Prostate Cancer Clinical Trials Consortium, Prostate Cancer Project) intended to accelerate translation from laboratory findings to clinical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of life and overall health and wellness
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve quality of life to enhance outcomes and overall health and wellness for those impacted by prostate cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the program's Overarching Challenges is to prioritize research that addresses quality-of-life issues and psychosocial/wellness outcomes for patients and caregivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new or improved treatments for lethal prostate cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop new treatments or improve upon existing therapies to improve outcomes for men with lethal prostate cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCRP places emphasis on therapies and therapeutic development aimed at lethal or advanced prostate cancer with the goal of reducing mortality and improving survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce prostate cancer disparities among high-risk groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce prostate cancer disparities among high-risk groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly seeks research addressing disparities (for example, noting African American men experience the highest incidence and mortality rates) and projects that target health equity and high-risk populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define biology of progression to lethal prostate cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the biology of prostate cancer progression to lethal prostate cancer to reduce death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCRP prioritizes mechanistic and biological studies that clarify the processes leading to lethal disease, with the goal of informing interventions to reduce mortality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to Service Members, Veterans, families, and military populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be relevant to Service Members, Veterans, and their families and consider the impact of prostate cancer on military populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program mission emphasizes benefiting U.S. Service members and Veterans (noting a high proportion of active duty personnel are men and historical prostate cancer diagnoses among service members); alignment to military health priorities and populations is a stated program focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with PCRP strategic plan and Overarching Challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should align with the PCRP strategic plan and address one or more of the program's Overarching Challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCRP developed a strategic plan to address critical gaps in prostate cancer research and patient care; applicants are expected to demonstrate how their proposals address the program's stated challenges (quality of life, therapies for lethal disease, disparities, biology of progression).
